### 2026-10-07 — Routing finished, DRC cleanup & Arduino IDE setup

**0.83h**

Routing finished, DRC cleanup & Arduino IDE setup

Hi, I'm Lincoln and I'm building Starbie, a tiny motion-controlled desktop pet (basically a Tamagotchi) for the Half Life starter project.

Quick context: I was so excited about this project that I just read the guide on GitHub and jumped straight into KiCad without exploring the Half Life site first. In that first session I did the whole schematic (importing the care package libraries, assigning footprints) and started the PCB: star-shaped board outline and component placement. I didn't know about Lapse yet, so that session wasn't recorded. After that I learned how journaling and timelapses work here, so from now on every session gets recorded.

What I did today (recorded):
- Finished the PCB routing (0 unconnected items in the DRC )
- Worked through the DRC violations: a malformed courtyard on the OLED footprint (J2)
- Set up the Arduino IDE for the XIAO ESP32-C3 following the guide and added the firmware sketch to the repo. I can't upload it yet since I don't have the board, but it compiles

Next:
fix the remaining DRC errors, export the 3D render and the Gerbers, then start working on the firmware.

### 2026-10-07 — DRC fixed, first look at the firmware, Gerbers & BOM exported

**1.12h**

DRC fixed, first look at the firmware, Gerbers & BOM exported

I started this session by fixing the other main DRC error on my PCB . Then I played around with
the firmware a bit to understand how it works. I can't upload it yet since
I don't have the XIAO ESP32-C3, but I wanted to get familiar with the code
before the board arrives.

After that I generated the Gerbers and drill files, exported the BOM as a
CSV, and pushed everything to my GitHub repo for Half Life.

Next: render the board in 3D and start writing my own firmware for Starbie.

### 2026-10-07 — ##Catching up: unrecorded work from my first sessions

**3h**

##Catching up: unrecorded work from my first sessions

In this entry I'm logging the work I did before I started recording with Lapse, so it couldn't be filmed.

Sorry about that: I hadn't read the docs all the way through, so I didn't know Lapse was the way to track hardware work. I lost quite a lot of time trying to track my KiCad hours with Hackatime and the kicad-wakatime extension, but it didn't work properly (it only sent heartbeats when I saved, so most of my time wasn't counted, like just 2 min was recorder). Then I read the journaling docs and understood that Lapse was the solution. Every session from now on is recorded.

**Discovering the project.** I went through the Starbie guide on GitHub and downloaded the Week 1 care package.

**Repository setup.** I created the GitHub repo, wrote a README with a schematic screenshot, set up a `.gitignore` for KiCad's temporary files, and connected the repo to Half Life.

**Schematic.** I added the care package libraries to my KiCad project (symbols and the `Imported Parts.pretty` footprints) and drew the schematic: XIAO ESP32-C3, OLED and MPU6050 on I2C, DHT11 with a 10k pull-up, and two Cherry MX switches. I replaced `SW_MEC_5G` with `SW_Push` because it had 4 pins for a 2-pad footprint.

**PCB.** I assigned the footprints, fixed the "footprint not found" errors by adding the footprint library, then drew the star-shaped board outline, placed the components and made a first GND ground plane.

guide, repo setup, schematic, footprints, board outline and placement, all done before I was recording.

**Next:** since the 3D part starts in week 2, I'll keep improving and personalizing my PCB, then work on the firmware to customize my Tamagotchi.
